requirements.statement: SceneAxi is one interactive engine/library ecosystem with separately versioned Game, Web Experience, and Kids profiles over one runtime and authoring core.
The monorepo uses strict downward package and surface boundaries, with exhaustive allow and deny lists.
Individual games remain outside this monorepo and consume versioned SceneAxi releases from separate repositories.
All shared contracts live in schemas, which has zero internal dependencies.
Profiles are independently versioned and each profile manifest carries a supported core-version range.
The core train, contracts, profiles, CLI protocol, identity, billing, and site packages use their declared release-group rules without implicit migration.
Delayed engine packages and additional provider slots remain pre-declared without being represented as shipped implementations.
requirements.classificationReason: The slots are reserved by the specification and are not packages on disk.

requirements.statement: The CLI exposes deterministic exit codes, versioned machine-readable envelopes, strict JSON mode, and next-action hints at every command level.
Authoring validation refuses schema major mismatches, unknown flags, ambiguous input, and partial-write risk, using atomic temporary-file replacement where mutation is allowed.
The E1 project command group provides new, one-shot dev, test, capture, and report verbs over canonical text documents.
Inspector edits use propose, review, and apply; no editor writes the canonical document directly.
Evidence-native test, capture, and report operations emit reproducible evidence packets with stable paths and model descriptors where applicable.
Web and desktop shells render the same protocol operations and produce identical canonical documents and evidence for equivalent edits.
Project dev watch remains a named refusal because the normative E1 hot-reload loop is not implemented.
requirements.classificationReason: The one-shot project dev path exists, but the specified watch loop is absent.

requirements.statement: Every held-key-gated CLI verb establishes the authoritative registry epoch before local checks and has no offline exception.
Held-key enforcement refuses unavailable currency, epoch drift, missing or stale snapshots, schema or map mismatch, undeclared verbs, open keys, and unknown keys.
Held-key acceptance includes both the fresh client epoch versus authoritative epoch bump regression and the unavailable-authority regression.
The Game Kernel public seam is open, dispatch, advance, observe, save, and replay, with only advance allowed to mutate.
The open path above the kernel resolves one host, stamps a deterministic bootstrap record, turns kernel throws into named refusals, and closes each handle once without a job system.
Kernel digests remain portable and browser-safe, with no Node builtins or Node-only globals in the kernel source.
Scene composition binds at least two placed instances to validated artifacts, preserves artifact bytes and evidence, and fails closed on its named refusal matrix.
The shared open-path policy is one data identity across CLI, profiles, desktop shell, and web shell; Kids is refuse-only and shippingClaim is false.
One Three presentation core serves a WebGL pixel surface and a deterministic headless surface, while no Three type crosses package exports.
Headless frames identify that no pixels were drawn; frame counters, tests, and gate output never imply a pixel or GPU claim.
The contained asset manifest admits only declared bounded profiles, derives stable identity and preview metadata from bytes, and reloads through review without mutating accepted bytes.
Native project creation writes the canonical document and v1 manifest atomically; legacy projects stay byte-identical until an approved migration commits.
Authoring transactions are base-versioned, atomic, recoverable, restart-durable, and support multi-level undo/redo with superseded redo invalidation.
Hierarchy, ordered multi-select, explicit-policy parenting, protected-root rules, and stable object identities project from the validated composed scene.
Transforms use one review command for numeric fields and gizmo nudges, with explicit local/world, pivot, axis, and snap inputs and no preview write before acceptance.
Prefab-like reusable content has versioned definitions, deterministic instances, explicit overrides, refresh behavior, and source-conflict refusals.
Unified input actions cover keyboard, pointer, wheel, and controller contexts with defaults, conflict checks, rebind/reset review, and restart-durable settings outside document undo.
Play uses an isolated clone bound to an explicit source hash; viewport sources switch through one owner and stop/reset never write authoring bytes.
Animation commands author bounded clips, tracks, and keyframes; scrub is non-mutating and deterministic replay uses the same catalog and hash.
Physics commands author deterministic bodies, shapes, materials, constraints, gravity, and a fixed 1–32ms step; animation precedes physics when both affect an object.
Environment, material, and seeded decorative-effect authoring stays presentation-authored, bounded, digest-stamped, and independently Kids-refusable.
Game and Web Experience profiles expose their bounded R1 open paths through the shared core; the Kids shared engine path is R0 refuse-only.
The Web Experience profile covers interactive site shells, hero scenes, configurators, storytelling, microsites, and data-driven real-time experiences, not CMS or SaaS behavior.
Kids safety is compiled into an isolated profile and site: no dependent package, identity, telemetry, cookies, commerce, or third-party LLM route may be introduced by a runtime toggle.
The Kids isolated activity is the only shipped Kids surface; it uses its own allowlist and in-memory activity and is not a consumer of shared profile or site packages.
The Model Provider Port is provider-neutral, capability-typed, per-profile filtered, and refuses absent policy, adapter, or capability before dispatch.
OpenRouter-first is the locked default for eligible non-Kids lanes, while DeepSeek use remains conditional, pinned, residency-bound, no-fallback, and outside strict tool-calling lanes.
requirements.classificationReason: Fixture and packaged BYOK paths exist, but no general production provider or credential authority is present in core.

requirements.statement: The catalog is one modular platform under two independently branded Game and Web storefronts with separate taxonomy, curation, branding, origins, and product surfaces.
Catalog intake proceeds quarantine to screening to human curation to listing and delisting/takedown, with every transition recorded and fail-closed.
requirements.classificationReason: The TEST-only editor intake connection is implemented; the production moderation operator and store are deliberately absent.

requirements.statement: Catalog items carry rights, provenance, mandatory AI disclosure, compatibility metadata, format profiles, and recorded moderation evidence.
requirements.classificationReason: The bounded fixture listing and contract metadata exist; marketplace listing and moderation activation remain held.

requirements.statement: Commerce fields remain inert until the existing per-storefront activation holds open; Kids consumption is an allowlist over already-curated items, never a pipeline fork.
requirements.classificationReason: The 6b marketplace activation and Kids safety branch remain separate authority holds.

requirements.statement: Identity, credits, and billing use injected Better Auth, Neon, and Stripe adapters; provider clients stay out of hermetic core.
Admin identity is derived only from normalized SCENEAXI_ADMIN_EMAIL; User has no role field that can be claimed by input.
Hosted login and logout require same-origin proof before fields or identity ports are reached, store the raw grant only in the HttpOnly session cookie, and keep redirects same-site.
Credit balance is derived from an append-only ledger; every store is created through the commit boundary and sale settlement commits both legs and the creator record atomically.
Hosted AI is default-off, follows the documented Kids → route → opt-in → ledger → replay → entitlement → metering → provider → debit order, and BYO remains free.
Checkout grant persistence acknowledges only after the ledger commit succeeds, and signed webhook evidence is bound to the exact Checkout Session and persisted intent.
Live Stripe mode has one environment authorization source and remains unavailable without its explicit audited authority; mode, environment, and key prefixes cannot authorize it.
requirements.classificationReason: The authorization resolver exists, but the repository does not authorize live activation.

requirements.statement: The desktop shell derives modes, controls, tabs, refusals, assistant states, and tiers from the shared editor-shell vocabulary and counts every control exactly once.
Standalone desktop chrome opens no kernel or presentation runtime and refuses runtime-dependent Open, Save, and Play controls by name.
requirements.classificationReason: The standalone shell is intentionally a visual projection without a packaged host.

requirements.statement: The packaged Linux desktop owns the application, bridge, renderer, project lifecycle, and local/BYOK assistant paths without adding a second product implementation.
First launch binds no project root and writes no project; roots enter only through a validated native dialog or recent registry.
The local agent bridge is a same-user Unix socket with a closed versioned tool and permission registry; every call validates capability, permission, and exact input before the desktop bridge.
Provider credentials never cross CLI arguments, tool input, RPC, discovery, logs, evidence, project documents, or the engine bridge; local and BYOK routes carry no credit route.
Ship → Export Web writes a contained content-addressed static viewer and Delivery Handoff without deploying.
macOS and Windows wrappers stage the Linux runtime but do not claim a public signed artifact or enable updates without real release inputs.
requirements.classificationReason: Packaging and refusals exist; signed/notarized public artifacts are absent.

requirements.statement: The umbrella editor constructs no canvas before identity and entitlement access succeeds; browser controls change URL state and never mutate engine state client-side.
The desktop assistant supports deterministic Local and injected BYOK paths, while Hosted refuses because this tier owns no identity or credits.
requirements.classificationReason: Local and BYOK are bounded; hosted metering is intentionally unavailable in this tier.

requirements.statement: The root quality gate fails when build, test, lint, sites, desktop, contracts, boundaries, or publish-readiness checks fail; passing while required stages are unwired is itself a regression.
Stage 1 proof remains separate from product presentation and requires both tier-3 captain decisions and explicit run authorization; no product implementation counts as proof evidence.
requirements.classificationReason: The proof program is referenced but no Stage 1 execution or adjudication is authorized.

requirements.statement: Review, apply, install, commit, push, merge, proof execution, spend/accounts, and publication are separate non-transitive authorities.
Production activation is a runbook only; external changes require a current authorization naming the exact action, target, scope, inputs, and rollback, and unchecked actions remain held.
requirements.classificationReason: The repository contains the procedure but no production action authority.

requirements.statement: Runnable claims use R2 startable, R1 driveable, and R0 refuse-only levels, each backed by a real entrypoint or named refusal and its highest available proof.

The CLI, catalog activation, Kids launch, package publication, license selection, Stripe LIVE, marketplace, and unsigned platform releases remain deferred or held until their separate authorities and evidence exist.
requirements.classificationReason: These are explicit out-of-scope or no-public-artifact conditions, not missing implementation tickets.

requirements.statement: The current Electron GPU-process crash on the local host is recorded as a host limitation; CI Xvfb/SwiftShader evidence owns packaged-runtime claims.
requirements.classificationReason: The current host crashes before SceneAxi proof; this does not establish a product defect.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/auth
requirements.statement: @sceneaxi/auth may use only the internal dependencies declared for its identity-port package.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/authoring-core
requirements.statement: @sceneaxi/authoring-core may use only its declared downward schemas and engine dependencies and remains the single authoring core.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/billing
requirements.statement: @sceneaxi/billing may use only its declared internal dependencies and contains no provider client dependency.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/catalog-game
requirements.statement: The dormant Game catalog app may depend only on schemas and its declared surface dependencies.
requirements.classificationReason: The catalog app is present for the delayed storefront track and is not an active product surface.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/catalog-web
requirements.statement: The dormant Web catalog app may depend only on schemas and its declared surface dependencies.
requirements.classificationReason: The catalog app is present for the delayed storefront track and is not an active product surface.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/cli
requirements.statement: The CLI may depend on authoring-core, schemas, and the bounded importer seam, but not directly on engine packages.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/desktop-linux
requirements.statement: The Linux desktop install root owns privileged Electron and provider adapters while unprivileged modules cannot reach them.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/desktop-macos
requirements.statement: The macOS packaging root stages the Linux runtime and cannot fork product behavior or publish without release prerequisites.
requirements.classificationReason: The packaging root and refusal path exist, but no signed public artifact exists.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/desktop-shell
requirements.statement: The desktop shell may use only schemas and authoring-core and must not import presentation, profile, site, or billing implementations.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/desktop-windows
requirements.statement: The Windows packaging root stages the Linux runtime and requires explicit signing and draft-release authority before upload.
requirements.classificationReason: Host-independent packaging checks exist, but no signed public artifact exists.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/engine-kernel
requirements.statement: The browser-runnable kernel may use only its declared downward dependencies and no Node-only runtime surface.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/engine-orchestrator
requirements.statement: The orchestrator may depend only on the kernel and schemas and owns no job queue or scheduler.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/engine-presentation
requirements.statement: The presentation package hides all Three types behind its public seam and may not name Node or DOM-only dependencies.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/importers
requirements.statement: Importers may depend only on schemas and authoring-core and retain the bounded contained-content projection.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/plugin-host
requirements.statement: The plugin host depends only on schemas and never reaches engine packages or a service locator.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/profile-game
requirements.statement: The Game profile may use only its declared core/profile dependencies and pins its core range.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/profile-kids
requirements.statement: The Kids profile has no undeclared dependents and its safety boundary remains structurally closed.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/profile-web
requirements.statement: The Web Experience profile may use only its declared core/profile dependencies and pins its core range.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/provider-openrouter
requirements.statement: The OpenRouter adapter stays fixture-tested with injected transport and does not own credentials or production readiness.
requirements.classificationReason: Adapter plumbing is real; live credential and production readiness are intentionally absent.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/schemas
requirements.statement: Schemas has no internal dependency and is the only shared contract/seam vocabulary package.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/site-catalog-game
requirements.statement: The Game storefront install root may use site-kit and its own provider surface without importing identity/billing or engine packages.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/site-catalog-web
requirements.statement: The Web storefront install root may use site-kit and its own provider surface without importing identity/billing or engine packages.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/site-kids
requirements.statement: The Kids site has an empty SceneAxi allow list and cannot import shared profiles, site-kit, identity, billing, or external data paths.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/site-kit
requirements.statement: Site-kit remains framework-free shared behavior and may not import React, Next, provider clients, or engine implementations.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/site-umbrella
requirements.statement: Only the umbrella site may depend on auth, billing, and engine-presentation, and privileged provider access is limited to the identity-plane plug point and adapters.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/web-shell
requirements.statement: The local web shell may use authoring-core and its explicitly declared auth/billing view-model edges but remains loopback-only and cannot reach engine sessions.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/cli
requirements.statement: The CLI is R2 startable from its built binary and has a spawned smoke proof.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/desktop-shell
requirements.statement: The desktop shell is R2 startable from its built binary and standalone chrome command.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/web-shell
requirements.statement: The web shell is R2 startable on loopback and exposes the existing inspector and assistant transport.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/desktop-linux
requirements.statement: The packaged Linux desktop is R2 startable with contained New/Open/Recent lifecycle and bounded editor paths.

requirements.subject: Game profile single-object open path
requirements.statement: The Game single-object profile open path is R1 driveable through the public seam.

requirements.subject: Game profile scene open path
requirements.statement: The Game multi-object scene profile open path is R1 driveable with checked-in replay evidence.

requirements.subject: Web Experience profile
requirements.statement: The Web Experience profile open path is R1 driveable through the public seam.

requirements.subject: Kids shared engine open path
requirements.statement: The shared Kids profile open path is R0 refuse-only and exposes no kernel, commerce, identity, or provider session.
requirements.classificationReason: The shared engine path is intentionally denied; the isolated Kids site owns a separate activity.

requirements.subject: Kids isolated activity
requirements.statement: The isolated Kids activity is R1 driveable only from its own site and shipped policy.

requirements.subject: Importers and plugin host
requirements.statement: Bounded importers and the first-class plugin host are R1 driveable through their checked public paths.

requirements.subject: Umbrella live open path
requirements.statement: The public umbrella /open path is R1 driveable and its headless proof does not claim pixels.

requirements.subject: Umbrella entitled editors
requirements.statement: The umbrella /editor projections are R1 driveable only after their access decision succeeds.

requirements.subject: @sceneaxi/desktop-macos
requirements.statement: The macOS packaging root is not yet an R2 surface because no signed artifact or packaged launch proof exists.
requirements.classificationReason: Packaging checks exist, but the signed release prerequisite and launch proof are absent.

requirements.subject: catalog applications
requirements.statement: The catalog applications remain dormant until the websites/deploy track and activation authorities open.
requirements.classificationReason: The apps are deliberately not active product surfaces.
